title: Feedback mesh anatomy: compact synthesis & request constellations
body:
Purpose
This doc is a compact, field-ready synthesis of customer feedback gathered May 10–May 28, 2026. Goal: turn noisy signal into a small set of request constellations (clustered asks) with suggested acceptance criteria and low-friction next steps for eng/product to triage.

Methodology
- Inputs: 42 support threads, 6 enterprise onboarding calls, two dedicated-customer postmortems, and telemetry snippets (p95 latency spikes, token-cost anomalies) pulled by CS.
- Cluster method: quick affinity grouping by impacted surface (latency, cost, rollout control, observability, private deploy blockers).
- Quick confidence score: high / medium / low (based on volume + severity + reproducibility).

Topline summary (1-paragraph)
Customers are asking for clearer runtime guarantees and simpler knobs to trade cost vs. quality for inference. Three friction points dominate: (1) sudden latency regressions on long-context chat sessions, (2) opaque cost spikes from unexpected tokenization/reprompt patterns and embedding reruns, and (3) rollout control/debugging gaps when a pinned model variant degrades in quality. These produce urgent asks from enterprise accounts and repeated operational tickets from PLG users.

Cluster A — Long-context latency regressions (confidence: high)
Representative quotes:
- "We saw our chat 99th percentile jump from 450ms to 1.8s when kernels swapped — hard to pin down why." — fintech beta
- "When a user sends a 4k token prompt, sometimes one request goes 5–10x slower than the next identical one." — marketplace app
Pain: unpredictable tail latency undermines SLAs and user-facing flows.
Requests (clustered):
1) tail-latency telemetry per-model-variant and per-seq-len bucket (acceptance: p50/p95/p99 broken out by seq-length bins; surfaced in Console).
2) automatic fallback policy with metricized switch: if p95 > X ms for N minutes, route to lower-cost variant or region (acceptance: configurable policy, 1-min cooldown, opt-in per-customer).
3) KV-cache warm/diagnostics endpoints (acceptance: per-customer cache hit rate, recent eviction log, simple API to pre-warm prefixes).
Effort/impact (opinion): medium effort, high impact for enterprise churn.
Owner suggestions: eng-serving-runtime + eng-sre for telemetry; product to spec fallback UI.

Cluster B — Cost surprises (confidence: high)
Representative quotes:
- "Embed jobs blew through quota because a downstream job re-embedded the same docs repeatedly." — data company
- "Quantization guidance we tried doubled cost for short prompts because batching dropped accidentally." — ML platform team
Pain: customers lack transparent unit accounting and tooling to prevent accidental reprocessing.
Requests:
1) token-level cost breakdown in billing UI + per-invocation attribution (acceptance: line-item export that maps invocation -> token counts -> model variant).
2) soft guardrails for large batch/embedding jobs (acceptance: threshold alerts + confirm step + recommended batching params).
3) sample prompts audit trail (acceptance: store user-provided prompt hashes for 7 days, show duplicates causing rework).
Effort/impact: low–medium effort, medium impact on cost-related support volume.
Owner suggestions: finance-ops + console team for UI; customer-success for guardrail wording.

Cluster C — Rollout/debugging gaps (confidence: medium)
Representative quotes:
- "We rolled a canary and saw hallucination rate spike only for our internal prompts; no easy way to compare side-by-side outputs." — enterprise search
- "When we pinned to an older version we couldn't see what kernel/runtime the host used." — healthcare customer
Pain: customers need deterministic comparison tools and clearer provenance for model/runtime pairing.
Requests:
1) per-rollout diffs (acceptance: automated sample set run against both variants; diff view in Console with metrics and example pairs).
2) execution provenance: model_variant -> kernel selection -> hardware instance id (acceptance: traceable field on each request for 30 days).
3) canary abort API (acceptance: programmatic kill + auto-rollback on metric delta).
Effort/impact: medium effort, high impact for enterprise confidence during upgrades.
Owner suggestions: product-console + eng-runtime.

Cluster D — Private deployment onboarding blockers (confidence: medium)
Representative quotes:
- "On-prem install failed because the KMS flow wasn't mirrored in our HSM testbed." — regulated infra
- "We need a one-page checklist for networking and ports to open — onboarding took 3 days longer than expected." — midmarket customer
Requests:
1) Private quickstart: condensed checklist + reference terraform module (acceptance: 1-page check, terraform module repo link).
2) HSM/KMS troubleshooting guide with common error signatures and example logs (acceptance: doc + sample logs + remediation steps).
Effort/impact: low effort, medium impact on reducing onboarding time.
Owner suggestions: private-deployments + solutions-eng.

Cross-cutting micro-asks (low-friction wins)
- Better default prompts for eval sets (impact: reduces false-positive regressions in rollouts).
- Console: short-lived links to specific request traces for sharing in CS tickets (impact: accelerates TTR).
- SDK: small example showing recommended batching/quantization pairing for short vs long prompts.

Risk signals / escalations
- Two long-standing enterprise accounts have flagged potential procurement pause if tail latency not addressed within Q3.
- One PLG customer showed a reproducible cost leak (embedding requeue) causing >$3k unexpected monthly spend; immediate guardrails recommended.

Proposed next steps (practical)
1) Triage workshop (1.5h) with eng-runtime, eng-sre, product-console, and 3 CS account owners. Goal: pick 2 pilot items (one high-impact: tail-latency telemetry, one low-friction: cost guardrail). Owner: Sofia (CS) to schedule.
2) Ship quick telemetry delta: add seq-len bins to existing p95/p99 export for two frequently used models (pilot customers only). Target: 6-week spike. Owner: eng-serving-runtime.
3) Fast guardrail: a console banner and threshold alert for embedding jobs over X docs / Y tokens. Target: 2-week spike. Owner: console-and-rollouts.
4) Create a one-pager private-deploy checklist and HSM troubleshooting stub; hand off to solutions-eng for validation. Target: 1 week. Owner: private-deployments.

Notes to reviewers
- This is intentionally terse; we collected many microthreads and intentionally collapsed similar asks to avoid duplication. Please flag anything we merged incorrectly.
- If product wants a different confidence rubric (e.g., weight by revenue instead of count), call it out in workshop prep.

Appendix (evidence snippets)
- Attached snippets in linked_artifacts: CONFLUENCE-4821 contains the 42 raw threads; JIRA-INF-723 is a backlog ticket created during triage; slack:#cs-field-notes has timestamped quotes.

Ownership & cadence
- CS will reopen this doc after the triage workshop with committed dates and ticket IDs.
- Suggested cadence: weekly check-ins for 6 weeks for pilot items, then monthly for rollout/debt items.

End of brief
